## Project Overview

This research examines the challenges
affecting social housing provision in
Ireland, with particular attention to
housing affordability, institutional
constraints, and alternative models
of housing development.

The project builds upon my legislative
internship with TD Mark Wall in the
Irish Parliament during summer 2026.

## Policy Problem

Many low- and moderate-income households
in Ireland face significant challenges
accessing affordable and suitable housing.

The issue extends beyond housing supply,
encompassing development costs,
institutional limitations, and barriers
to accessing social housing.

## Research Methods

My research incorporates several
approaches, including:

- Policy and legislative analysis
- Interviews with housing policy experts
- Review of academic literature
- Comparative analysis of housing models
- Examination of institutional barriers

## Key Areas of Research

### Local Authority Capacity

Examining the role of local authorities
in the financing, development, and
management of social housing.

### Housing Affordability

Investigating the relationship between
housing costs, household incomes,
and eligibility for housing supports.

### Alternative Housing Models

Exploring international approaches to
affordable housing provision, including
cost-rental housing and Vienna's
social housing model.

## Research Progress

This project is ongoing.

Additional findings, analysis, and
recommendations will be added as
the research develops.
